findings.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:119 — The `conditions.reduce((acc, condition, index) => index === 0 ? condition : Prisma.sql\`(${acc}) AND (${condition})\`)` AND-joining pattern is duplicated verbatim (with OR variants) at lines 171 and 204, and should be extracted into a shared `joinSql(conditions, "AND"|"OR")` helper to avoid triple maintenance.

packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:99 — Column names like "eventTypeId", "eventParentId", "userId" are now hardcoded string literals in raw SQL instead of typed `Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` keys, so a future Prisma schema rename will silently break these queries at runtime with no compile-time signal.

packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:151 — buildOrgAuthorizationCondition hardcodes "teamId" and "isTeamBooking" as raw SQL strings, losing the compile-time safety that Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput previously provided against column drift.

packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:196 — buildTeamAuthorizationCondition duplicates the same hardcoded "teamId"/"isTeamBooking"/"userId" column-name strings seen in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, compounding the drift risk since any schema change must now be hunted down across multiple string literals instead of caught by the type checker.

packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:68 — Removing the `findMany()` wrapper in favor of exposing `getBaseConditions()` pushes the responsibility of constructing raw SQL (table name, SELECT columns, embedding the returned Prisma.Sql fragment) onto every future caller, whereas the old API only required passing a typed Prisma `where`/`findMany` args object.

packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:29 — InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` duplicates the shape of the discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` but with all scope-specific fields optional and no scope-based narrowing, so callers get no compile-time guarantee that e.g. `teamId` is present when `scope === "team"`, reintroducing the type-safety problem the discriminated union was meant to prevent.

packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:481 — The new usage pattern for getBaseConditions() is a raw `$queryRaw` SELECT with no LIMIT/pagination, and since the prior findMany() wrapper (which allowed take/skip via Prisma args) is gone, every future caller must now hand-write LIMIT/OFFSET themselves, creating an easy-to-miss unbounded-query risk.

packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:349 — The "Caching" describe block ("should cache authorization conditions", "should cache filter conditions") was deleted with no replacement, so caching of the new Prisma.Sql-based cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions fields is now completely untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:119 — The `conditions.reduce((acc, condition, index) => index === 0 ? condition : Prisma.sql\`(${acc}) AND (${condition})\`)` AND-joining pattern is duplicated verbatim (with OR variants) at lines 171 and 204, and should be extracted into a shared `joinSql(conditions, "AND"|"OR")` helper to avoid triple maintenance.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the same `conditions.reduce(...)` pattern used multiple times to join `Prisma.Sql` fragments: in `buildFilterConditions()` to AND-join (`return Prisma.sql\`(${acc}) AND (${condition})\``) and in both `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition()` and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition()` to OR-join (`return Prisma.sql\`(${acc}) OR (${condition})\``). This is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability issue (duplicate logic), not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:99 — Column names like "eventTypeId", "eventParentId", "userId" are now hardcoded string literals in raw SQL instead of typed `Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` keys, so a future Prisma schema rename will silently break these queries at runtime with no compile-time signal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces typed `Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` objects with `Prisma.sql` fragments that hardcode column identifiers like `"eventTypeId"`, `"eventParentId"`, `"userId"`, `"teamId"`, etc. (e.g., in `buildFilterConditions()` and `buildAuthorizationConditions()`). This is verifiably true from the change and does reduce compile-time protection against Prisma schema/field renames, potentially causing runtime breakage later, but it is not an immediate, demonstrable defect introduced by the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:151 — buildOrgAuthorizationCondition hardcodes "teamId" and "isTeamBooking" as raw SQL strings, losing the compile-time safety that Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput previously provided against column drift.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes authorization conditions from Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput to raw SQL (Prisma.sql). In buildOrgAuthorizationCondition it now builds conditions like Prisma.sql`("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)` (and similar for "userId"), which hardcodes column names as strings. This does lose the compile-time/type safety previously provided by Prisma’s typed where input against schema/column drift. This is a real maintainability/robustness concern introduced by the change, but not a directly verifiable functional bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:196 — buildTeamAuthorizationCondition duplicates the same hardcoded "teamId"/"isTeamBooking"/"userId" column-name strings seen in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, compounding the drift risk since any schema change must now be hunted down across multiple string literals instead of caught by the type checker.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes authorization/filter logic to raw SQL via `Prisma.sql` and hardcodes column names as string literals in multiple places. For example, `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` constructs SQL with `"teamId"`, `"isTeamBooking"`, and `"userId"` strings, and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` repeats the same column-name strings in its own SQL fragments. This duplication increases schema-drift/rename risk compared to the prior typed `WhereInput` approach, and it’s a concrete maintainability concern introduced by the change, not an immediate functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:68 — Removing the `findMany()` wrapper in favor of exposing `getBaseConditions()` pushes the responsibility of constructing raw SQL (table name, SELECT columns, embedding the returned Prisma.Sql fragment) onto every future caller, whereas the old API only required passing a typed Prisma `where`/`findMany` args object.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)` and replaces it with `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>` (see `insightsBooking.ts` around the old `findMany` implementation). The integration test is updated to manually run `prisma.$queryRaw` with `SELECT ... FROM "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" WHERE ${baseConditions}`. This confirms the API shift: callers must now choose the table, select list, and embed the returned `Prisma.Sql` fragment themselves, instead of passing typed Prisma `findMany` args. That’s an API/architecture ergonomics concern introduced by the change, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:29 — InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` duplicates the shape of the discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` but with all scope-specific fields optional and no scope-based narrowing, so callers get no compile-time guarantee that e.g. `teamId` is present when `scope === "team"`, reintroducing the type-safety problem the discriminated union was meant to prevent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` with `scope: "user" | "org" | "team"` but `teamId?: number` optional, and changes the constructor to accept this type (`options: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`) instead of the discriminated-union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`. This removes compile-time narrowing/guarantees that `teamId` is present when `scope === "team"`, even though `setOptions` still parses into the stricter Zod discriminated union at runtime. That’s a real, diff-grounded type-safety/API regression concern, but not a directly verifiable runtime defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:481 — The new usage pattern for getBaseConditions() is a raw `$queryRaw` SELECT with no LIMIT/pagination, and since the prior findMany() wrapper (which allowed take/skip via Prisma args) is gone, every future caller must now hand-write LIMIT/OFFSET themselves, creating an easy-to-miss unbounded-query risk.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `findMany()` from `InsightsBookingService` and replaces it with `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>` (insightsBooking.ts). In the integration test, the new pattern is `prisma.$queryRaw` with `SELECT id ... WHERE ${baseConditions}` and no `LIMIT` (insightsBooking.integration-test.ts around the updated block). While this isn’t a verifiable correctness defect in the diff itself (the test dataset is small), it is a concrete API/usage change: callers can no longer pass Prisma `findMany` args like `take/skip` through the service wrapper and must now craft their own queries (often via raw SQL), making it easier to accidentally write unbounded queries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:349 — The "Caching" describe block ("should cache authorization conditions", "should cache filter conditions") was deleted with no replacement, so caching of the new Prisma.Sql-based cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions fields is now completely untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the entire `describe("Caching")` block in `insightsBooking.integration-test.ts` (tests for caching authorization and filter conditions) and does not add any new tests that exercise the caching behavior. Meanwhile, `InsightsBookingService` still implements caching via `private cachedAuthConditions?: Prisma.Sql;` and `private cachedFilterConditions?: Prisma.Sql | null;` with memoization in `getAuthorizationConditions()` / `getFilterConditions()`. So the caching logic for the new Prisma.Sql-based fields remains but is no longer explicitly tested.
